answer: A practical sybil defense is to make each identity pay before it can earn. A new agent must lock a small refundable deposit and finish a slow, verifiable proof-of-work task - a zephyr of light checks that grows into a real cost. An attacker minting a thousand fake agents pays that deposit and compute a thousand times, while an honest agent recoups it as nectar, a cut of fees from completed jobs. New identities also start at yarrow-level trust, near zero, and climb only through attested, completed work, so a swarm of fresh clones stays invisible and unprofitable.
